title: Ordinary alteration topology and marked regular-cover predicate
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme with a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use the category $\operatorname{alt}/S$ of [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], whose underlying category is independent of its prime parameter. Its objects are finite-type morphisms $T\to S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $T$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], such that every generic point of an irreducible component of $T$ maps to a generic point of a component of $S$ and the induced residue-field extension is finite [def-weil-irreducible-components], [def-weil-residue-field]. A generic point of a component is a point whose closure is that component. Morphisms are the $S$-morphisms. The ordinary alteration topology is the smallest Grothendieck topology [def-weil-pbc-topos] in which the sieves generated by jointly surjective etale families [def-weil-etale-morphism] and by singleton proper surjective morphisms in this category [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism] are covering. The sieve generated by a family consists of the arrows factoring through a member of that family; the family is covering when this sieve is covering. A family $(A_j\to S)_j$ refines $(T_i\to S)_i$ if there are indices $i(j)$ and $S$-morphisms $A_j\to T_{i(j)}$.

For reduced $S$ and a nowhere dense closed subset $Z\subset S$, write $U(S,Z)$ for the proposition that there is a finite ordinary alteration covering $(T_i\to S)_i$ with each $T_i$ nonempty integral regular Noetherian [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-regular-scheme], and with the set-theoretic inverse image of $Z$ equal to the support of a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. The boundary is allowed to be empty. An empty covering family is allowed when $S$ is empty. No prime or invertibility condition is part of these definitions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q51-fad29930b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The delivery is one commit with the item and its report. Compared with the base in clones/side-live, only status (unsplit to split), five new searches and the split_report changed; the statement and its 14 stmt_deps are byte-identical, there are no new nodes and no proof. I read ILO in the local PDF. II 1.2.2 with 1.1.2 and 1.1.8-1.1.9 at parameter 1 gives the item's objects of alt/S: finite type, reduced source, generic points of components going to generic points with finite residue extension. II 1.1.10/1.2.3 says every morphism of alt/S is maximally finite dominant, so generator (ii) is just a proper surjective morphism. II 2.1.1 at parameter 1 makes generator (i) a jointly surjective etale family. II 2.3.1-2.3.3 and Remark 2.3.2 support taking the smallest Grothendieck topology, which is well defined as the intersection of all topologies containing the generators. VII Theorem 1.1 asks for regular connected X_i; this matches the item's nonempty integral regular Noetherian T_i, because the T_i are Noetherian and connected regular Noetherian schemes are integral, and empty members can be dropped since the empty sieve covers the empty scheme. All 14 deps define what is used. The alt/S paragraph of def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology agrees word for word, and its topology needs a prime, so this item is not a duplicate. No other definition node or blueprint node gives the alteration topology. The users apply U to reduced or integral S. Edge cases checked: S empty, Spec k, reducible S. No fixes, no tool_uses.

lean.statement: def topology (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S] : GrothendieckTopology (PrimeToEllAlteration.Alt S)
lean.note: Reuses PrimeToEllAlteration.Alt and PrimeToEllAlteration.Refines without a prime parameter. The additional definitions give ordinary generators, the least topology, covering families, the canonical reduced base object, and U(S,Z).

reviewed_lean.note: Node changes only in its lean record. The module adds five definitions, no sorry, with source and blueprint docstrings. It reuses PrimeToEllAlteration.Alt and Refines. The topology is the smallest one generated by jointly surjective étale presieves and single proper surjective morphisms, with no prime condition, matching ILO II at parameter 1. U(S,Z): S reduced, Z closed with empty interior, a finite Fin n cover of the identity base object, members integral, regular and Noetherian, with an SNC boundary whose support equals the preimage of Z.
